actions.name: Exploit JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2023-42793 for initial access
actions.description: The SVR started to exploit Internet-connected JetBrains TeamCity servers in late September 2023 using CVE-2023-42793, which enables bypassing authorization and arbitrary code execution on the server.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Execute arbitrary code with high privileges on TeamCity server
actions.description: The TeamCity exploitation usually resulted in code execution with high privileges granting the SVR an advantageous foothold in the network environment.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Perform host reconnaissance using built-in commands
actions.description: The SVR used basic built-in commands such as whoami, nltest, tasklist, netstat, and wmic to perform host reconnaissance.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Exfiltrate files from compromised hosts
actions.description: The SVR exfiltrated files such as ntoskrnl.exe, SQL Server executable files, Visual Studio files, and update management agent files to gain insight into the host system and software.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Compress Microsoft SQL Server DLL files using PowerShell
actions.description: The SVR used PowerShell commands to compress Microsoft SQL Server DLL files into a zip archive.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Disable or kill endpoint detection and response (EDR) and antivirus (AV) software using 'Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver' technique
actions.description: The SVR used an open source project called EDRSandBlast to remove protected process light (PPL) protection and inject code into AV/EDR processes to evade detection.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Hide backdoors via DLL hijacking and masquerading
actions.description: The SVR abused DLL hijacking vulnerabilities in Zabbix and Webroot software and backdoored an open source Microsoft application named vcperf to hide backdoors.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use Microsoft OneDrive and Dropbox cloud services as covert C2 channels
actions.description: The SVR used Microsoft OneDrive and Dropbox cloud services to exchange data with malware hidden inside randomly generated BMP files.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Perform privilege escalation using WinPEAS, NoLmHash registry modification, and Mimikatz
actions.description: The SVR used multiple techniques for privilege escalation including WinPEAS, modifying the NoLmHash registry key, and executing Mimikatz commands.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Establish persistence using scheduled tasks
actions.description: The SVR relied on scheduled tasks to secure persistent execution of backdoors, storing executables in various Windows directories and using schtasks.exe to create tasks.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Craft Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs) using Rubeus toolkit
actions.description: To secure long-term access to the environment, the SVR used the Rubeus toolkit to craft Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs).
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Exfiltrate Windows Registry hives
actions.description: The SVR exfiltrated Windows Registry hives SYSTEM, SAM, and SECURITY by saving them to files, compressing them, and exfiltrating using backdoor capability.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use SharpChromium tool to obtain sensitive browser data
actions.description: In a few specific cases, the SVR used the SharpChromium tool to obtain sensitive browser data such as session cookies, browsing history, or saved logins.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Perform network reconnaissance using built-in commands and PowerSploit
actions.description: The SVR performed network reconnaissance using built-in commands and PowerSploit commands executed in memory, such as Get-NetComputer, Get-NetGroup, Get-NetUser, Get-NetDiDomain, Get-AdUser, and Get-DomainUser.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Establish tunnel to C2 infrastructure using modified Rsockstun tool (rr.exe)
actions.description: The SVR used a modified open source reverse socks tunneler named Rsockstunp (rr.exe) to establish a tunnel to the C2 infrastructure, executed either in memory or using WMIC.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Perform lateral movement using WMIC and registry modification
actions.description: The SVR used WMIC to facilitate lateral movement by executing commands remotely and modified the DisableRestrictedAdmin registry key to enable remote connections.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use GraphicalProton backdoor for C2 communication
actions.description: The SVR used the GraphicalProton backdoor, which uses OneDrive, Dropbox, and randomly generated BMP files to exchange data with the SVR operator. It gathers environment information and uses cloud services as primary and backup communication channels.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use GraphicalProton HTTPS variant for C2 communication
actions.description: The SVR introduced a variant of GraphicalProton backdoor that uses HTTPS requests to a re-registered expired domain with a dummy WordPress website as C2 channel, split into stager and encrypted binary files.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.
